ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, and authorized traders against: (i) domestically and internationally designated politically exposed persons and heads of international organizations per FINTRAC guidance; (ii) Canadian consolidated sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and the Sergei Magnitsky Law; (iii) Criminal Code section 83.05 terrorist entity listings; (iv) OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions for all USD-denominated clearing; and (v) the UN Security Council Consolidated List. Enhanced due diligence is triggered because ISIC 4669 covers wholesale of waste and scrap, a commercially sensitive circular-metals channel; the sponsoring bank will additionally require documentary LC terms, original invoices, scale-weight notes, and independent surveyor certificates for each consignment. Re-screening must occur at inception, on any ownership or authorized-signatory change, and at least annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Register; online service 'Demande de réservation d'un nom' available at https://registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the corporate name must be in French form; a non-French distinctive element may be retained only when combined with a French generic component (e.g., 'Recyclage', 'Commerce', 'Gestion') of at least equal prominence. A bilingual name is accepted when a distinct French version exists and the French component is not subordinate. Non-Latin scripts require a statutory Latin-alphabet transliteration in French, together with the mandatory legal designation 'Société en commandite', 'S.E.C.', or 'L.P.'. No foreign fantasy names without a French generic term will be reserved.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection is communicated in writing by the REQ within five business days with the stated grounds. The applicant may file a written administrative review under section 31 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1) within 30 days of the refusal; the review is assigned to the director's delegate and is decided within 30 days. If denied again, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of Québec under articles 529 et seq. of the Code of Civil Procedure (CQLR c. C-25.01), filed within 30 days of the second refusal. Alternatively, a fresh reservation bearing a modified distinctive element may be submitted immediately with the original rejection reference; the REQ processes reconsideration requests within 10-15 business days. A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 90 days upon payment of the statutory extension fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted: the Quebec Limited Partnership must maintain a real establishment (établissement) in Quebec, reflected in the REQ declaration of registration, where statutory books, registers, and PCMLTFA record-keeping are physically accessible. A pure virtual mailbox without a physical records location is not acceptable for an operational scrap-metal trading partnership. A serviced office with an assigned physical suite, trade-name signage, and local personnel satisfies commercial-substance and REQ requirements; a shared co-working hot-desk is generally insufficient for non-ferrous metals consignment operations but may be tolerated for a passive holding vehicle.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 25-35% annual probability of an unannounced on-site compliance inspection by Revenu Québec, FINTRAC-programmed examinations of the sponsoring bank, or municipal metal-dealing licensing authorities; probability increases to approximately 45% where the partnership files for GST/HST and QST input tax credits on cross-border consignments or becomes an object of a bank-submitted suspicious transaction report.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss 2, 15, 25, 26, 44; Civil Code of Québec, arts 2236-2243 (limited partnership constitution and liability).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Enterprises of Quebec), www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration – Limited Partnership (Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or pledge requirement under the Civil Code of Québec. Limited partners' liability is limited to their agreed contribution as stated in the limited partnership agreement and the declaration. A prudent capital level should be maintained to satisfy the scrap-metal dealer permit bonding and commercial counterparty requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporate general partner approves and ratifies the formation of the limited partnership (société en commandite) under the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; that the registered office shall be established at [address], Quebec; that the contribution of the general partner, as set out in the limited partnership agreement, is accepted as the subscribed partnership capital; and that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and General Manager, each with authority to file the declaration of registration, to publish required notices, to open banking accounts, and to execute agreements. All proceedings are approved and confirmed effective forthwith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online name search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary search of the Quebec enterprise register to confirm the proposed name is distinctive and does not reproduce a protected name. Submit a name reservation application for the limited partnership, including the legal designation 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' (or 'L.P.' in English). The reservation is valid for 120 days and must be referenced in the subsequent declaration of registration. Online submissions use a click-wrap attestation; paper filings require notarized signature or attached written mandate.
required_dossiers: Proposed name including appropriate legal suffix
Name reservation application form
Identity and contact details of applicant
Authorization or agency mandate if filed by a third party
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar refuses the name as non-distinctive or contrary to law, file a written response containing additional arguments or alternative names. For refusals based on prohibited terms, request a formal review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, and ultimately appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Foundation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des notaires du Québec / legal counsel; corporate general partner's board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement (acte de société) identifying the general and limited partners, capital contributions, profit sharing and management powers. Draft and execute the Declaration of Registration – Limited Partnership before a Quebec notary or with notarized signatures of the general partner's authorized representative. The corporate general partner must adopt the pro-forma first board resolution approving the formation. The declaration must state the partnership's legal designation and the name and address of the general partner.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement
Declaration of Registration – Limited Partnership
First board resolution of the corporate general partner
Certified copy of the general partner's certificate of existence and bylaws (if the general partner is a corporation)
Notarial attestation of signature (required for paper filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registrar identifies incomplete information, amend and re-sign the declaration. If a partner is omitted, file an amending declaration. No penalty is imposed if the correction is made within 30 days after the enquiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration Filing with the Registraire des entreprises (REQ)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online fiscal centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Declaration of Registration through the REQ online portal or in paper form at an REQ office. Pay the registration fee of CAD 42 (approximately USD 31 as of 2025). The REQ will issue the certificate of registration and assign the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). The registration is published in the register and becomes opposable to third parties with respect to the partnership's legal form and partner identification.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration
Proof of payment of registration fee
Name reservation certificate (if reserved)
Schedule of general partners and value of contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the online filing fails validation, review the error report, correct formatting issues, and refile. For a paper refusal, submit an amended declaration. Request an express review of any contested entries through REQ's internal complaint procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Customs and Employer Registrations with Revenu Québec and CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the NEQ, register with Revenu Québec for the QST and GST accounts (unless the supply is confirmed zero-rated) and, if the partnership has employees, for employer health-services and CNESST assessment accounts. A customs-specific registration with the Canada Border Services Agency is recommended for cross-border consignments of shredded non-ferrous scrap. This registration also establishes the partnership's rights and duties for tax collection and remittance.
required_dossiers: Copy of the REQ certificate of registration
Quebec enterprise number (NEQ)
Business address and mailing address
Tax identification details of general and limited partners
Expected revenue and supply description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrations are queried by Revenu Québec, provide supplementary documentation within the statutory delay. A default assessment may be contested by a notice of objection under the Tax Administration Act (CQLR c A-6.002).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Scrap-Metal Dealer Permit and Operational License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal borough / Service de police; Ministère de la Sécurité publique; local fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the scrap-metal dealer's operating permit required under the Act respecting the sale and resale of metals (chapter V-1.5). Submit business and plot plans, criminal record declarations, a site storage plan, a waste management and recycling procedure, and proof of validation by the local fire safety department. This permit is mandatory for physically handling, storing, or consigning scrap copper and other non-ferrous metals. The environmental compliance clearance (EIA registration or exemption) is obtained in parallel from the ministry of environment.
required_dossiers: Scrap-metal dealer permit application form
Criminal record checks for principal owners and managers
Site lease or ownership deed and plot plan
Fire safety certificate
Waste handling and emergency response plans
EIA registration or preliminary compliance decision
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused or conditioned, submit a written explanation or revised site plan. Appeal to the municipal council or the competent administrative tribunal. If the refusal is arbitrary or exceeds jurisdiction, apply for judicial review at the Cour supérieure du Québec (Superior Court of Quebec).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Sécurité publique (permit authority for metal recovery) and the applicable municipal borough / Service de police.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permit for Metal Recovery Operators (Permis de récupérateur de métaux) under the Act respecting the sale and resale of metals, CQLR c V-1.5.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 'Registration' (preliminary declaration of compliance) for a storage and transhipment yard handling shredded non-ferrous scrap; 'Exempt' for an office-only brokerage function or if storage is below the regulatory tonnage threshold without any thermal or chemical processing. A full environmental impact assessment is triggered only by smelting, refining, or other high-risk thermal/metal treatment operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Must comply with the Regulation respecting the discharge of industrial effluents (Q-2, r. 19) – wastewater pH 6.0–9.5, suspended solids ≤ 600 mg/L, aluminum ≤ 5 mg/L, iron ≤ 8 mg/L, copper ≤ 2.0 mg/L, no visible oil and grease. Volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions from any cutting or cleaning line must remain below 10 kg/day to avoid an air-approval requirement. Hazardous residues (scrap contaminated with oil, PCBs or other substances) must be characterized and disposed of in accordance with the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (Q-2, r. 32).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the local fire service under the Regulation on fire safety, including access routes, extinguishers, storage separation, and emergency response plan. Structural load inspection by a professional engineer for racking, shelving and scrap stockpiles. Occupational health and safety clearance from CNESST under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1), including accident prevention program, first-aid equipment, and workers' compensation registration. Local municipal building permit and zoning compliance certificate for warehouse and loading areas.

mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A / CAERS electronic export report)
Packing List and Scrap Grade/Weight Certificate
SWIFT MT103 / Documentary LC presentation evidence (bank proof of foreign remittance)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange-control regulator. The central bank operates monetary policy, currency issuance, the Retail Payment Activities Act registration function, and payment-system oversight, while the Department of Finance and FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) administer cross-border fund-transfer reporting and AML/CTF obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada has operated without exchange controls since the Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951, so neither the Bank of Canada nor any other agency must approve profit remittance, capital repatriation, or currency conversion involving the CAD. For the Quebec Limited Partnership, the practical hurdles are limited to: (1) Part I income tax on each non-resident partner's share of the partnership's Canadian-source business income, because the LP is a permanent establishment of each partner for tax-treaty purposes; (2) Part XIII withholding at 25% (treaty-reduced) on payments that are in substance interest, royalties, or management fees; (3) FINTRAC electronic funds transfer (EFT) reporting by the bank for any cross-border wire of CAD 10,000 or more received or sent within a 24-hour period; and (4) bank-side source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification. There is no Quebec-specific convertibility or repatriation restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement for export proceeds. The LP may retain USD or EUR proceeds in foreign-currency accounts indefinitely and convert at the prevailing market rate. Mandatory non-surrender obligations remain: (1) export reporting to the CBSA through the Canadian Export Reporting System for commercial shipments, including HS 7404.00 copper waste and scrap; (2) bank-filed FINTRAC EFT reports for international transfers of CAD 10,000 or more within 24 hours; and (3) proper accounting for foreign-exchange gains and losses on the LP's Canadian-dollar books. Exports of HS 7404.00 scrap are not on Canada's Export Control List, so no Global Affairs Canada permit is required except where the goods or destination are sanctioned.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada) - Schedule I
Desjardins Group (Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / FX and trade hedging line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM, strictly conditional. A foreign or offshore EMI (for example, Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, or MultiPass) may lawfully move CAD on behalf of the Quebec LP only if the EMI (1) is a registered money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC, (2) holds the Quebec money-services business licence of the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) where it carries on business in Quebec, and (3) holds a payment service provider (PSP) registration with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act if it provides open-loop payment functions. No offshore EMI can issue or confirm documentary letters of credit or provide true escrow-grade clearing for HS 7404.00 scrap cargoes. The EMI may function only as a supplementary FX/liquidity gateway; the statutory LC, escrow, and CAD-clearing rails must remain with a Schedule I bank or a licensed Canadian credit union for this trade profile.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC's client-identification rules permit remote verification using a recognized trusted digital-identity service, so there is no absolute statutory requirement that all directors or partners appear physically in Canada. In practice, the LP should assume a de facto mandatory in-person interview for the general partner's authorized signatory at the primary Montreal branch because (1) non-ferrous scrap wholesaling is a known trade-based money-laundering typology; (2) the ownership base includes non-resident partners; and (3) the entity is newly capitalised. Remote video onboarding is accepted only with documented compliance-committee approval and appointment of a Canadian-resident compliance contact or a Quebec-licensed corporate-service provider as agent for service. Non-resident partners must supply apostilled registry extracts, notarized passport copies, and independent legal-opinion letters confirming corporate authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags in copper scrap and shredded non-ferrous metal trading: over/under-invoicing, mixed-metal bales, weight variance, cash-intensive suppliers, and unstable LME pricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete per-transaction trade file: LME Grade A copper price curve with a documented scrap discount; calibrated weighbridge tickets; XRF or spectrometer assay certificates; source supplier invoices and supplier KYC files; chain-of-custody and transport manifests; CBSA export declarations; board-approved no-cash and no-bearer-instrument policy; quarterly internal AML file reviews; independent accountant review of trade economics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership: a Quebec Limited Partnership with foreign general and limited partners creates UBO tracing risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: REQ declaration of registration (immatriculation); executed limited partnership agreement and register of partners; UBO register identifying every individual holding 25% or more of any class of partnership interest; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for each non-resident partner; tax identification numbers; foreign-counsel legal opinions on legal existence and signing authority; annual AML attestations of all partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire velocity and value spikes inconsistent with a modest working-capital envelope or with the stated trade cycle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy with a wire pre-approval matrix; LC-backed disbursement path; complete MT103/MT202 trail; monthly reconciliation of wires against commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and CBSA export records; two years of audited financial statements or a review-engagement statement if newly formed; rolling cash-flow model supporting the expected wire pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and origin-of-goods risk: scrap copper may conceal embargoed or conflict-origin metal or involve sanctioned counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ongoing name-and-entity screening against Global Affairs Canada Canadian sanctions, UN, OFAC, EU, and UK sanctions lists; certificate-of-origin and non-conflict declarations from each seller; HS 7404.00 classification memorandum; contractual end-user and anti-diversion covenants; bank-approved counterparty whitelist; Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) for operating counterparties; customs-broker confirmation of lawful export.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from non-resident partners is routed by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV where interbank cover is required) to the LP's segregated operational/capital escrow account at National Bank of Canada in Montreal. No Bank of Canada or CRA authorization is required. Mandatory protocol: use the LP's exact legal name and Quebec NEQ registration number in the beneficiary field; include payment reference 'LP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' with the supporting capital-call clause number; pre-notify the relationship manager for any wire above CAD 100,000 with the executed capital-call notice, partner resolutions, and source-of-wealth pack so the bank can file the required FINTRAC EFT Report without a compliance hold; maintain the LP books in CAD functional currency using the settlement-day exchange rate; and, for partner loans rather than equity, execute an arm's-length credit agreement with market-rate interest to avoid deemed-interest issues and to document Part XIII withholding and treaty analysis.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails are layered: (1) documentary import-commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 opened at the LP's bank for supplier shipments, payable at sight or tenor against presentation of transport documents (bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, assay certificate, and certificate of origin), which provides the strongest TBML-resistant rail; (2) direct SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for freight, customs duties, insurance, and pre-approved suppliers on the compliance whitelist; (3) MT202 COV cover payments where the beneficiary bank requires a separate cover leg; (4) CAD domestic legs settled same-day through Payments Canada's Lynx high-value payment system; and (5) a bank-approved prohibition on cash, bearer instruments, undocumented third-party payments, crypto rails, and non-whitelisted EMI transfers. Each disbursement must cite the underlying purchase contract or LC number and reconcile to CBSA export declarations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/CNH) up to 24 months with a Schedule I bank or authorized derivatives dealer under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and USD/EUR) fully collateralized under the bank's standard CSA
Vanilla FX options and zero-premium collar structures limited to purchased protection on documented USD receivables and payables
CME-listed CAD/USD futures and USD-denominated copper futures (HG) as exchange-traded synthetic hedges
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only where the sale contract settlement currency is non-convertible or restricted and only through a globally regulated bank; never permitted for CAD
Window forwards and rolling hedging programmes aligned to the monthly LME copper-indexed receivable cycle

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Updating Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing charge of CAD 16 applies for declarations submitted after the 60-day window; continued non-filing can trigger a formal notice and administrative strike-off (radiation) from the Quebec enterprise register, terminating the LP's public legal personality and limited-partner liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013 and Quebec provincial equivalent TP-600)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (federal) and Revenu Québec (provincial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 5 months after the partnership fiscal year-end for non-calendar periods; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, due no later than the applicable T5013/TP-600 filing deadline (generally March 31). Mandatory only if the limited partnership meets the active-business, partner-count, or asset-value thresholds under the federal Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a required partnership information return attracts CRA late-filing penalties of CAD 25 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500, plus interest on unpaid amounts; Revenu Québec imposes corresponding administrative penalties for late or omitted TP-600 filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatorily required for a privately held limited partnership under the Quebec Civil Code or Quebec Business Corporations Act. An independent audit becomes compulsory only if the limited partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities law, is required by its partnership agreement, or is contractually obligated by banking or lending covenants.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable or reporting-issuer limited partnerships; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for private non-reporting limited partnerships.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's annual updating declaration requires confirmation of the limited partnership's principal address and the names and addresses of its general partners. There is no separate annual UBO confirmation filing for a private limited partnership; any corporate general partner is independently responsible for maintaining a significant-control register and filing its own corporate annual confirmations under the applicable corporate statute.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: No statutory registers are mandatory for a Quebec limited partnership; the LP should retain its limited partnership agreement, partner meeting minutes, and financial and tax records for CRA, Revenu Québec, and Quebec enterprise registrar audit purposes.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 650 - CAD 1,500 per year (USD 480 - USD 1,100) for a registered office and registered agent in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 for a medium trading and distribution limited partnership when an audit is required; no audit fee applies if the partnership is not audited
